name: B10-0116/2025 (Renew) – Further deterioration of the political situation in Georgia
title: JOINT MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the further deterioration of the political situation in Georgia
part_text:
The European Parliament calls on the European Union and its member states to reject the current Georgian government, which it says took power through flawed elections. It asks for new free elections, the release of people detained in protests, and sanctions on officials blamed for cracking down on protesters, journalists and opposition leaders. It also wants the European Union to keep recognising Salomé Zourabichvili as Georgia's legitimate president and to give more money to Georgian civil society and independent media.

- The European Union and member states are asked to refuse to recognise the current Georgian parliament and president, and to impose sanctions on officials.
- Georgian officials, judges, media propagandists and Bidzina Ivanishvili are the targets of the proposed sanctions and travel limits.
- The European Union is asked to review Georgia's visa-free travel and redirect funding to civil society; the parliament's position is not binding.
